nuggets.text: The Bobcats won the first FCS title game ever to go to overtime, edging Illinois State 35-34 in January.
Taco Dowler caught the 14-yard overtime touchdown that won the Bobcats the national championship.
Justin Lamson was named MVP of the FCS title game after leading the Bobcats past Illinois State.
The Bobcats closed last season with 14 straight wins, the last one in overtime for the national title.
Jabez Woods returned a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown in the Bobcats' 51-24 win over Butler.
Montana State is the only program with national titles at three levels: NAIA, Division II and FCS.
The Bobcats shared the 1956 NAIA national title after a 0-0 tie with St. Joseph's in the Aluminum Bowl.
Nevada coach Jeff Choate led the Bobcats from 2016 to 2019, taking them to the FCS semifinals in 2019.
Bobcat great Jan Stenerud came from Norway on a ski jumping scholarship and became the first pure kicker in the Hall of Fame.
Bobcat Stadium opened in 1973 as Reno Sales Stadium, named for the college's only graduate of 1898.
